measure: aggregate forecast year for a 50% chance of high-level machine intelligence (HLMI)
notes: Grace et al., 2016 Expert Survey on Progress in AI, paper at arXiv 1705.08807. Paper states 'the aggregate forecast gave a 50% chance of HLMI occurring within 45 years'; 2061 = survey year 2016 + 45 (conversion ours; matches the plan's 2061). Definition given to respondents: 'High-level machine intelligence (HLMI) is achieved when unaided machines can accomplish every task better and more cheaply than human workers.' Aggregation: each respondent's three points fitted to a gamma cumulative distribution by least squares; 'Aggregate Forecast' is the mean distribution over all individual distributions, read at 50% - not a median of answers, so not directly comparable with Müller and Bostrom. Half got fixed-years framing (probability by a given year), half fixed-probabilities framing (year for a given probability); 'we simply average over the two framings'. Sample: all researchers who published at NIPS and ICML 2015; 1634 contacted, 352 responded (21%); responses May 3 to June 28 2016. n left blank: number answering the HLMI question is not stated in what was read (most of the 352; a subset got the full-automation question instead).

measure: aggregate forecast year for a 10% chance of high-level machine intelligence (HLMI)
notes: Paper states the aggregate forecast gave 'a 10% chance of it occurring within 9 years'; 2025 = 2016 + 9 (conversion ours). measure: aggregate forecast year for a 50% chance of full automation of labour
notes: Paper: 'the mean of the individual beliefs assigned a 50% probability in 122 years from now'; 2138 = 2016 + 122 (conversion ours). The abstract rounds this to 120 years.
